title: **Why is the U.S. pursuing such a system?**
text:
"**Why is the U.S. pursuing such a system?**"

"Subsurface warfare is one of the most complex areas of military operations. The underwater environment, unlike the sky and the earth's surface, limits the possibility of constant and easy communication, and detecting a subsurface vehicle is far more difficult. For this reason, the use of unmanned systems can reduce some of these limitations. An autonomous vehicle can remain in a specific area for a long time, collect information, and carry out its mission without putting crew members' lives at risk. The Dive-LD is fundamentally designed for exactly this purpose."

"**The significance of the capture**"

"The IRGC's statement specifically mentions "intelligence and operational dominance." This phrase carries special meaning in subsurface operations. Detecting and intercepting an unmanned underwater vehicle—especially a system designed for independent operations—requires a set of intelligence, reconnaissance, and subsurface environmental monitoring capabilities."

"The Dive-LD incident should not be viewed merely as a one-off operation. The main significance of this event lies in the fact that it shows the future of warfare will not be solely about missiles and manned aircraft; a significant portion of military competition will shift to underwater environments, autonomous systems, artificial intelligence, sensors, and electronic warfare. In modern warfare, sometimes the most valuable victory is not the destruction of a system, but its discovery, control, and acquisition—because in the latter case, the enemy not only loses an operational tool but also exposes some of its technological secrets to study.
